title: improv·artist · elemental (Olafur Eliasson)
mutation_directive: improv artist: elemental via Olafur Eliasson

improv_extras.practice: weather as art; light, water, ice, fog; the room becomes the medium

v1.feedback: The Weather Project ring-sun concept reads clearly within 2 seconds and the sodium-vapor amber palette is a genuinely restrained, idea-driven choice — good execution of the Eliasson brief. However, the form is essentially a flat orbiting disc; adding a mirror-plane reflection (Eliasson's actual trick — a half-disc mirrored on the ceiling) would elevate it from 'ring of particles' to unmistakable Weather Project homage. The residual strange-attractor perturbation (att * 0.008) adds subtle turbulence but doesn't read as fog or atmosphere — replace it with a periodic density modulation or radial fade that simulates haze layers receding in depth. Consider slowly rocking the camera or pulling it slightly off-axis so the disc's slight z-undulation becomes visible as atmospheric shimmer rather than staying hidden in the face-on view.

v2.feedback: The Weather Project homage lands well — sodium-vapor monochrome is the right call and the mirror-plane horizon is a direct Eliasson reference that reads in seconds. The disc form is recognizable but leans generic: it's a glowing orb, not weather-as-medium. Push the elemental concept further by breaking the perfect radial symmetry — add slow convection cells or asymmetric corona tendrils so the sun feels alive rather than procedural. The z-shimmer is too subtle at default camera distance; either pull the camera closer or increase the haze amplitude so the atmospheric depth Eliasson trades in actually registers on screen.
